recommendation: Keep the commit. It aligns the active Resource Guide and Task example index with the already-applied removal and current Financial Module guidance without editing historical or out-of-build artifacts.
issue_request: FHIR-19345 was Published/Persuasive for FM and requested removing ProcessRequest and ProcessResponse, adding comparable Task examples, and documenting Task use for the former ProcessRequest/ProcessResponse business purposes on the Financial page.
initial_application: GF #19345 commits in November 2018 added Financial Module Task documentation and financial Task examples, added supporting Task code/input terminology, and removed ProcessRequest/ProcessResponse from active build metadata, hierarchy, resource list, workflow, and status-code metadata. Current fhir.ini confirms those resources are commented out and listed only as removed/historical.
additional_context: The active Financial Module already documents Task for cancel, nullify, poll, release, reprocess, and status workflows. Current active source still had stale Resource Guide rows presenting ProcessRequest and ProcessResponse as current resources and Task example-list copy/paste labels that made several Financial examples appear to be cancel examples. FHIR-16924, Confluence workflow minutes, and a Zulip Resource Name Map thread support the removal and clarify that the historical use cases moved partly to Task and partly to RESTful query.
reconciliation: Changed active source by removing the ProcessRequest/ProcessResponse rows from source/resourceguide.html and correcting source/task/list-Task-examples.xml display labels plus the reprocess description. Left out-of-build resource folders and historical/reference artifacts unchanged.
source_changes: source/resourceguide.html: removed stale ProcessRequest and ProcessResponse rows from the active Order Management resource table.
source/task/list-Task-examples.xml: corrected Financial Task example display labels for poll, release, reprocess, status, and status response, and corrected the reprocess description.

related_jiras.note: Earlier ProcessRequest/ProcessResponse objection resolved no-change after the resources had been removed; it supports the end state but was not decided separately.
